title: Oculomotor delayed response
summary: Funahashi, Bruce & Goldman-Rakic's (1989) oculomotor delayed-response task: hold fixation while a square flashes for 0.5 s at one of eight locations 13 deg out, keep fixating through a 1.5-, 3- or 6-s delay, then, when the fixation spot goes off, saccade to the remembered location within 0.5 s. A landing within 6 deg (diameter) of the cue is correct. Human and monkey parameter sets and a monkey training ladder; the paper's neuronal recordings are not part of it.
references: Funahashi, S., Bruce, C. J., & Goldman-Rakic, P. S. (1989). Mnemonic coding of visual space in the monkey's dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Journal of Neurophysiology, 61(2), 331–349. https://doi.org/10.1152/jn.1989.61.2.331
Wang, X.-J. (2005). Discovering spatial working memory fields in prefrontal cortex. Journal of Neurophysiology, 93, 3027-3028 (secondary source).

deviations.original: Three adult rhesus monkeys, trained for 3-4 months (p. 332)
deviations.here: A monkey parameter set (configs/task-monkey.yaml) and a human parameter set (configs/task.yaml): the same trial, humans instructed (instructions.md) and never paid
deviations.reason: The classic is used with human volunteers as well; the two files differ only in their subject block (tests/test_configs.py)

deviations.original: Scleral search coil (Robinson's method), digitized at 500 Hz (pp. 332-333)
deviations.here: A video eye tracker (example rigs: EyeLink), gaze read once per display frame. A blink loses the eye on a video tracker, and alhazen counts a lost sample during fixation as a break, so a blink before the go signal ends the trial as FIX_BREAK (the coil kept measuring through blinks)
deviations.reason: Non-invasive and what most labs have; alhazen reads one gaze sample per frame

deviations.original: Online velocity-based saccade detection (van Gisbergen et al. algorithm) on differentiated eye position (p. 333)
deviations.here: Onset = the first frame gaze is outside the 1.5-deg fixation window; endpoint = the first new sample slower than 30 deg/s (alhazen's StimulusResponse and LandingSample)
deviations.reason: alhazen's frame-based gaze phases; latencies are quantized to frames and include the time to leave the fixation window

deviations.original: Monochrome 19-in. CRT subtending 48 x 38 deg, PDP-11/23 with a GRAPH-11 card (p. 332)
deviations.here: The rig's monitor through PsychoPy; durations rounded to whole frames; a screen that cannot show the 13-deg cues is refused
deviations.reason: Hardware; the paper's CRT is not available

deviations.original: Not stated in the paper; a dark screen in a dark room according to a later account (Wang 2005, p. 3028)
deviations.reason: alhazen v3.0 fixes the window colour at mid-grey; a dark field needs an alhazen capability (docs/methods.md, Verification)

deviations.original: Single-neuron recording in the principal sulcus and frontal eye fields, microstimulation to identify FEF sites (pp. 332-334)
deviations.here: Not included. Task events can drive TTL sync lines (configs/rig-gaze-example.yaml) for a lab's own recording system
deviations.reason: This folder is the behavioural task; the recording and stimulation systems are the lab's

deviations.original: 0.2-ml drops of lightly sweetened water via an electronic metering pump (p. 332)
deviations.here: A pulse train on the rig's reward line, set in the monkey file (or volume_ul once the rig's juice per pulse is measured)
deviations.reason: A pulse-driven line delivers a volume that depends on the pump; alhazen meters by pulses or by a measured volume per pulse

assumed.value: 1.5 deg radius (3 deg across), the same through fixation, cue and delay
assumed.reason: The paper gives no fixation window; chosen to tolerate video-tracker noise while keeping the eye near the spot

assumed.item: Time allowed to look at the fixation spot
assumed.reason: Not stated; a trial must end if the subject never looks

assumed.value: The first new gaze sample slower than 30 deg/s after gaze leaves the fixation window
assumed.reason: The paper used a velocity algorithm but gives no threshold; 30 deg/s is a conventional saccade-offset threshold

assumed.item: Wait for the eye to settle
assumed.value: 150 ms after saccade onset; if it has not settled, the last sample is judged
assumed.reason: Not stated; a 13-deg saccade lasts about 50 ms, so 150 ms leaves room without reaching a corrective saccade

assumed.value: 3 per block, 6 per session (144 completed trials)
assumed.reason: Not stated (the paper's data files held 50-100 trials, p. 333); 6 per cell gives a usable endpoint distribution in a 23-30-min session

assumed.value: Delays interleaved at random with the eight locations, each block a shuffled complete replicate
assumed.reason: The paper states only that location was randomized (pp. 332-333) and that delays were sometimes combined

assumed.value: 2 blocks with a rest (and a chance to recalibrate) between them
assumed.reason: Not stated; a rest halfway through a 23-30-min session

assumed.value: The saccade must start (gaze leave the fixation window) within 0.5 s of the go signal; its endpoint is judged when the eye lands
assumed.reason: "If the monkeys made a saccadic eye movement within the next 0.5 s" (pp. 332-333) does not say whether onset or landing must fall within 0.5 s

assumed.value: A trial ended by NO_FIXATION, FIX_BREAK or NO_SACCADE is served again later in its block; INACCURATE responses are kept and not repeated
assumed.reason: Not stated; repeating aborted trials keeps every cell filled, and keeping errors keeps the large-error trials the paper examined (p. 331, Summary 9)

assumed.value: Nothing is shown: the cue does not reappear, there is no feedback, and the trial ends at the landing
assumed.reason: The paper describes no feedback other than the reward
Not stated in the paper (a later account says the screen was dark, Wang 2005); alhazen v3.0 does not let a task set the window colour (also a deviation)

assumed.value: 1 pulse of 200 ms per CORRECT trial
assumed.reason: The paper gives a volume (0.2 ml), not a pulse train; the volume per pulse depends on the rig's pump and must be measured

assumed.value: fixate -> visually guided saccade (the square appears as the spot goes off) -> memory saccade with 0.25/0.5/1-s delays -> the full task, with the windows, response periods, trial counts, rewards and criteria in the ladder file
assumed.reason: The paper says only that training took 3-4 months (p. 332); this is the usual route to a memory-guided saccade

assumed.value: The wording in instructions.md; SPACE starts the session
assumed.reason: The paper's subjects were monkeys; humans need instructions

tasks.title: Oculomotor delayed response
tasks.summary: Fixate; a 0.5-s cue at one of eight locations 13 deg out; a 1.5/3/6-s delay with fixation held; the spot goes off; saccade to the remembered location within 0.5 s.

parameters.name: fix_size_dva
parameters.label: Fixation spot diameter
parameters.meaning: Diameter of the white fixation spot. Paper: p. 332.

parameters.name: cue_size_dva
parameters.label: Cue size
parameters.meaning: Side of the filled white square cue. Paper: p. 332.

parameters.name: cue_ecc_dva
parameters.label: Cue eccentricity
parameters.meaning: Distance of the cue's centre from fixation. Paper: p. 332, Fig. 2.

parameters.name: cue_angles_deg
parameters.label: Cue locations
parameters.meaning: Polar angles of the eight cue locations, counter-clockwise from the right (90 = up). Paper: p. 331, p. 332.

parameters.name: fix_window_dva
parameters.label: Fixation window radius
parameters.meaning: Gaze must stay within this radius of the spot until the go signal. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: target_window_dva
parameters.label: Response window radius
parameters.meaning: A saccade endpoint within this radius of the cue location is correct (6 deg diameter). Paper: pp. 332-333.

parameters.name: fixation_period
parameters.label: Fixation period
parameters.meaning: Fixation held before the cue. Paper: p. 332, Fig. 1.

parameters.name: cue_duration
parameters.label: Cue period
parameters.meaning: How long the cue is shown. Paper: p. 332, Fig. 1.

parameters.name: delays
parameters.label: Delays
parameters.meaning: The delays, one per condition, interleaved with the locations. The paper's three-delay combination (pp. 332-333); it usually used 3 s alone.

parameters.name: response_period
parameters.label: Response period
parameters.meaning: Time after the spot goes off within which the saccade must start. Paper: pp. 332-333 (reading it as a limit on the start is ASSUMED).

parameters.name: landing_settle_speed_dva_s
parameters.label: Saccade end speed
parameters.meaning: The endpoint is the first gaze sample slower than this after leaving fixation. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: landing_max_wait
parameters.label: Landing wait
parameters.meaning: How long after saccade onset to wait for the eye to settle. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: acquire_timeout
parameters.label: Fixation acquisition limit
parameters.meaning: Time allowed to look at the spot before the trial ends as NO_FIXATION. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: iti
parameters.label: Inter-trial interval
parameters.meaning: Blank interval between trials. Paper: p. 332.

parameters.name: paradigm.n_per_condition
parameters.label: Trials per condition per block
parameters.meaning: Completed trials of each location x delay per block. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: paradigm.blocks.n_blocks
parameters.label: Blocks
parameters.meaning: Blocks, with a rest between them. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

outcomes.name: CORRECT
outcomes.meaning: The saccade started within the response period and its endpoint fell within the 6-deg-diameter window around the cue location. A monkey is paid juice.

outcomes.name: INACCURATE
outcomes.meaning: The saccade started in time and landed outside the window (or its endpoint was not measured). Kept, not repeated.

outcomes.name: NO_FIXATION
outcomes.meaning: Gaze never reached the fixation window within the acquisition limit; served again.

outcomes.name: FIX_BREAK
outcomes.meaning: Gaze left the fixation window (or was lost) before the go signal; served again.

outcomes.name: NO_SACCADE
outcomes.meaning: Gaze did not leave the fixation window within the 0.5-s response period; served again.

events.name: FIX_ACQUIRED
events.meaning: Gaze entered the fixation window; the 0.75-s fixation period starts on the next frame.

events.name: FIX_OFF
events.meaning: Fixation spot off: the go signal; latency is measured from this flip.

events.name: LANDED
events.meaning: The saccade's endpoint was measured (the eye settled).

tasks.timeline: ITI 5 s | fixation 0.75 s | cue 0.5 s | delay 1.5/3/6 s | go: saccade within 0.5 s | landing
